name: Lapis Legit (Many-Layered Spiced Cake)
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
steps: Mix and sift cloves, cardamom, nutmeg, and cinnamon.
Beat butter until smooth and creamy.
Whip egg yolks with sugar until fluffy.
Whip egg whites in separate mixing bowl until fluffy, then mix with egg yolks.
Combine the spices, condensed milk, flour, and butter.
Using a small cup, spread 30–35 ml batter into the pan to make a layer.
Bake in preheated 350°F oven, heated from the top, until golden (4–5 minutes).
Remove from oven, brush with butter for flavoring, and top with another 30–35 ml batter to make another layer.
Repeat the baking and layering to make around 30–40 layers.

culture.text: Lapis legit, also known as spekkoek, and kueh lapis in Singapore, is a type of Indonesian layer cake. It was developed during colonial times in the Dutch East Indies. The firm-textured cake is a Dutch-Indonesian version of kue lapis, the multi-layered steamed rice cake common in Southeast Asia, but using Dutch ingredients like flour and butter. It contains a mix of Indonesian spices, such as cardamom, cinnamon, clove, mace and anise. The cake is made of flour and yolk and is rich in butter or margarine.
